text:
marta: FYI I opened a PR to move payments_module -> payments/v2 and pin the provider constraints per module. Plan looks mostly clean but one weird diff on the cred provider path. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123
alex: saw it, thanks. quick question: are we keeping a registry alias or doing a full module rename?
sam: full rename, but we want a shim for consumers for one release cycle so we can avoid mass PR churn. shim will be a tiny module that re-exports to payments/v2.
jit: sounds good. what about the provider block pins? current PR changes providers.tf in module root from `~> 3.2` to `>= 3.5, < 4.0` — is that bilateral with the root lockfile?
marta: right, I updated module-level required_providers for the module to the new constraints and regenerated the lockfile in the branch. I included the plan output for the canary namespace:```terraform plan -out=plan.bin``` plan says: ```-/+ module.payments.google_service_account.billing (local-exec): resource will be replaced``` don't want unintended replace.
alex: could be because of provider alias changes: earlier we used provider "google.billing", new module uses default provider and sets provider_alias in parent. If the alias mapping changes, terraform will want to replace resources bound to the old provider instance.
sam: can we keep provider alias and add compatibility provider block in the v2 module that references the alias? e.g., in payments/v2/main.tf: ```provider "google" { alias = "billing" }``` plus `providers = { google = google.billing }` in module block?
jit: that will work but you need to ensure the lockfile includes the same provider version constraints. I recommend setting the module's required_providers to be compatible with root, not stricter, then run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` to regen.
marta: good call. I tried regenerating but used the workspace that had pinned 3.5; maybe CI ran with older lockfile. I'll re-run with consistent env.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: plan validated on branch marta/module-payments-v2 — 3 warnings, 0 errors. Warnings: provider alias mapping may force replacement of 2 resources. Use `terraform state replace-provider` if you want to rebind without recreation.
alex: ooh, state replace-provider is an option but risky in prod. For staging we can do it. For a safer step, can we add a lifecycle rule to preserve the SA? e.g., `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = false }` not ideal.
sam: alternatively, do a small canary: deploy v2 to a test project, export state, use `state replace-provider`, run acceptance tests, then do the big swap.
jit: also double-check k8s secret paths: the module rename changes secret path from `secret/data/payments` to `secret/data/payments/v2` — most consumers read explicit path from module output. We should keep an output `secret_base_path` that defaults to `payments` for v1 and `payments/v2` for v2 and allow override via var.
marta: I'll add `variable "secret_base_path" { default = "payments/v2" }` and keep outputs `secret_path = "${var.secret_base_path}/keys"` then we can set var in consumers to maintain v1 path temporarily.
alex: (cc @jit) once you push the lockfile regen, can you also add a short note in the PR description about state replace-provider and the recommended canary steps? saves time for reviewers.
jit: will do. also include `terraform validate` and `tfsec` results in PR.
marta: pushing update in ~30m. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
alex: :eyes: ping me when it's ready, I'll quick-smoke the plan in staging.
sam: tagging sales infra owners too since production rollout touches billing SA. `@rebecca` FYI.
infra-bot: mention: @rebecca added to thread by sam.
